HIF-α signaling modulates the metabolic activity and cytokines released by human dendritic cell in response to the fungal pathogen A. fumgatus.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIF-α is a modulator for the anti-fungal response of human DC and that this effect is independent of the oxygen concentration.
HIF-α signaling modulates the anti-A. fumigatus immune defense initiated by human DC.
HIF-α signaling modulates the metabolic activity and cytokines release of human DCs in response to A.fumigatus, which may be relevant for the host defense and pathogenesis of invasive aspergillosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF- 1α modulated metabolic activity and cytokines in anti-A. f. umigatus immune responses of human DCs.
HIF-α modulates the metabolic activity and cytokines release in the anti-Aspergillosis immune response initiated by dendritic cells.
HIF-α signaling is involved in DC metabolism and cytokines release, and thus in DC function, which is of importance in A. fumigenus infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HIF- 1α is a relevant immune-modulatory factor in human DCs and that it contributes to metabolic activity and cytokines release in anti-A. fumi-gatus immune responses initiated under normoxic as hypoxic conditions.
HIF- 1α signaling in DCs modulates the metabolic activity and the cytokine release in the immune response against A. f.
HIF- 1α is an immune-regulatory transcription factor in human DC responses to A. f umigatus and that its function is dependent on the oxygen concentration of the culture medium.
